title: Power Integrity Intern Worker Engineer
description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
As a Physical Design Engineering Undergraduate Intern, you will actively contribute to the physical implementation of silicon and platform designs to ensure readiness for manufacturing. This role will provide hands-on experience in design flows, power integrity analysis, and validation activities for high-speed interconnect architecture. You will gain valuable skills, apply theoretical knowledge to practical projects, and explore future career opportunities while collaborating with a team of innovative engineers.
The Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE) drives innovation in silicon and platform design, ensuring the physical designs meet manufacturing and performance standards. The team focuses on delivering scalable, efficient solutions that align with Intel's broader goals of advancing technology and enabling cutting-edge products. Joining this group offers a collaborative environment committed to excellence in engineering and design.
The primary responsibilities for this role will include, but are not limited to:
Assist in the physical implementation of package and platform designs, contributing to power integrity and high-speed interconnect validation.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support design scalability, automation, and manufacturability.
Engage in verification and signoff processes to ensure compliance with performance and manufacturing standards.
Apply theoretical knowledge to practical projects, including power integrity analysis and physical design optimization.
Support design initiatives by leveraging advanced tools and methodologies to address technical challenges.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications :
Minimum qualifications are required to be initially considered for this position.
Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electronics or Electrical Engineering with at least 50 percent of coursework completed OR pursuing a Master's degree in the same field.
Bachelor's candidates must demonstrate 0-1 years of hands-on experience in physical design, with skills gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training. Master's candidates require no prior professional experience.
Proficiency in English (written and verbal).
Completion of at least 1-2 courses in Electrical/Electromagnetic fundamentals.
Maintain a minimum of 80 percent GPA.
Availability to work at least 22.5 hours per week during the internship period.
Commitment to work a minimum of 1 year in this position.
Legal authorization to work in Costa Rica.
Preferred Qualifications:
Preferred qualifications are in addition to the minimum requirements and are considered a plus factor in identifying top candidates.
Familiarity with electrical simulation tools such as Sigrity PowerSI, SiWave, Hspice, Matlab, or Ansys HFSS.
Experience with PCB design or circuit simulators.
Knowledge of statistical analysis tools such as JMP or equivalent.
Strong collaboration and analytical skills with an eagerness to learn and solve technical challenges.
Bring your passion for innovation and engineering to Intel-apply today and make your mark on the technology of tomorrow.

Student / Intern
